issues.evidence: P22_numeric_stats_with_NA_cell; csv_analytics.py:62 -> column v=[1,2,N/A,3] reports mean/median/stdev null
issues.summary: A single non-numeric cell (e.g. N/A) in a numeric column makes all numeric stats null without warning.

issues.evidence: P20_non_utf8_clean_error; output 'UnicodeDecodeError: utf-8 codec can't decode byte 0xff' traceback
issues.summary: A non-UTF-8 input file crashes with a traceback instead of a clean error (read_csv only catches FileNotFound/IsADirectory/Permission).
A UTF-8 BOM is kept in the first header name, so selecting or filtering on that column by its visible name fails.
An unwritable output path raises a traceback instead of a clean error.

issues.evidence: -o /nonexistent/dir/r.json -> FileNotFoundError traceback (csv_analytics.py:151 is outside the try)
issues.summary: An unwritable output path raises a traceback instead of a clean error.

issues.evidence: csv_analytics.py:154-160; default stdout is a text table
issues.summary: Stdout is a text table by default; you get JSON only with --json or -o, and the tool also adds unrequested extras (regex filter, multiple files, --rows).

blinding_guess.why: A ships a unit-test suite and a dedicated error class with tighter scope, which looks like spec-driven output, while B is a feature-rich single script with no tests.

notes: Both pass all core probes for stats, filter, select and JSON export. A fails three robustness probes: non-UTF-8 input gives a traceback, a BOM stays in the header name, and an N/A cell nulls a column's numeric stats. B handles all three. Neither side catches an unwritable --output path. The bandit reports are empty for both, and ruff shows only style findings (A: 20 including tests; B: 3).
